papers.title: Connecting bond switching to fracture toughness of calcium aluminosilicate glasses
papers.abstract: Fracture toughness is a critical mechanical property of glasses, but a detailed understanding of its link to composition and structure is still missing. Here, focusing on the industrially important family of calcium aluminosilicate glasses, we measure the fracture toughness of two glass series using the single-edge precracked beam method, one based on tectosilicate compositions with varying silica contents and the other covering both percalcic and peraluminous compositions with varying Al/Ca ratio. To elucidate the structural origins of the variation in fracture toughness, we perform X-ray total scattering measurements and molecular dynamics simulations. Our findings show that local coordination changes of especially Al atoms, so-called bond switching, feature an overall positive correlation with fracture toughness. We also compare this variation with that in other mechanical properties, including elastic moduli, hardness, and crack initiation resistance. We find that various structural aspects need to be considered to describe and understand the mechanical properties of calcium aluminosilicate glasses.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究钙铝硅酸盐玻璃断裂韧性的结构起源。
summary_zh.method: 使用单边预裂纹梁法测量断裂韧性，结合X射线总散射和分子动力学模拟。
summary_zh.result: 铝原子局部配位变化(键切换)与断裂韧性呈正相关。
summary_zh.validation: 实验测量和MD模拟相互验证。

summary_en.motivation: To understand the structural origins of fracture toughness in calcium aluminosilicate glasses.
summary_en.method: Fracture toughness measured by single-edge precracked beam method, combined with X-ray total scattering and molecular dynamics simulations.
summary_en.result: Local coordination changes of aluminum atoms (bond switching) show a positive correlation with fracture toughness.
summary_en.validation: Experimental fracture toughness measurements and molecular dynamics simulations provide complementary validation.
